title: What a harness is — the landscape
takeaway: Read a dated landscape along independent axes: source rights, provider choice, and interface, rather than a single product ranking.

scenes.title: The machinery around the model
scenes.visual: 1.1.1: diagram opens a cutaway with a fixed model core and surrounding planning, memory, perception, and action ring; gradeBadge A accompanies the survey grounding. 1.1.2: add context, tools, execution, state, policy, and orchestration as an explanatory synthesis, not an academic standard. 1.1.3: move CLI, editor, and web surfaces outside the harness boundary.

sentences.text: A coding model is not the whole agent: a peer-reviewed survey describes planning, memory, perception, and action around it.
Practitioners use harness for surrounding machinery: context, tools, execution, state, policy, and orchestration.
That is different from the interface where you watch and supervise the work.

onScreen.text: Model core → planning, memory, perception, action · survey-grounded agent components, not a universal harness taxonomy
Harness: context · tools · execution · state · policy · orchestration | Human surfaces: CLI · editor · web · explanatory synthesis

scenes.title: Useful, not settled vocabulary
scenes.visual: 1.2.1: quoteCard displays Chase's exact short quotation with attribution and dateStamp. 1.2.2: diagram gives framework, runtime, and harness overlapping outlines rather than hard nested boundaries.

sentences.text: In October 2025, LangChain's Harrison Chase described harness as a term gaining currency.
sentences.spoken: In October twenty twenty five, LangChain's Harrison Chase described harness as a term gaining currency.

sentences.text: He acknowledged blurry boundaries with frameworks and runtimes, and explicitly disclaimed inventing the term.

onScreen.text: “just starting to see be used more” · Harrison Chase on “Agent Harness” · October 25, 2025 · first-party terminology discussion, not a coinage claim

scenes.title: Independent axes, not a podium
scenes.visual: 1.3.1: diagram shows an unranked matrix with source rights, provider freedom, and interface columns. 1.3.2: place Codex CLI and Amp as dated example rows, not scored dots. 1.3.3: expand the Codex row into multiple surfaces and draw an ACP editor-to-agent boundary; use gradeBadge C and dateStamp throughout. 1.3.4: emphasize the provider-performance and component-license conditions already attached to the map.

sentences.text: Read this landscape along independent axes: source rights, provider freedom, and the work surface.
Codex CLI is open source with custom and local providers; Amp is proprietary but supports multiple models and provider connections.
OpenAI documents a shared Codex harness across surfaces, while Agent Client Protocol lets compatible editors host independently developed agents.
Provider choice does not guarantee equal performance; repository licenses and service terms have different scopes.

onScreen.text: As of 2026-10-08 · Codex CLI/core: Apache-2.0, custom/local providers | Amp: proprietary, multi-model, provider connections · licenses apply to named components, not every associated service
One Codex harness → multiple surfaces | Agent Client Protocol (ACP): compatible editor ↔ independent agent · documented compatibility, not equal performance across models

scenes.visual: 1.4.1: barChart reveals independent bars, never a pie, retaining denominator and overlapping-selections caption. 1.4.2: emphasize the overlapping-selections caption. 1.4.3: a separate trust panel shows its own question and population rather than stacking into the product chart. Keep gradeBadge C and dateStamp visible.

sentences.text: Stack Overflow's 2026 survey reports past-year use: Claude Code, 65.5%; Copilot, 58.7%; and Codex, 29.5%.
sentences.spoken: Stack Overflow's twenty twenty six survey reports past year use: Claude Code, sixty five point five percent; Copilot, fifty eight point seven percent; and Codex, twenty nine point five percent.

sentences.text: These are overlapping survey selections among respondents, not mutually exclusive market shares.
Trust is conditional: 48.0% trust easily verified output; only 6.6% trust AI with important work decisions, in a separate survey question.
sentences.spoken: Trust is conditional: forty eight percent trust easily verified output; only six point six percent trust A I with important work decisions, in a separate survey question.

scenes.title: Shared names, different boundaries
scenes.visual: 1.6.1: diagram places AGENTS.md and Agent Skills beside the agent as instruction inputs. 1.6.2: draw MCP to external tools/data, ACP to an editor, and A2A to a separate opaque agent application. 1.6.3: add a native internal-worker branch explicitly distinct from A2A. 1.6.4: retain the protocol map while highlighting the warning that common formats do not guarantee common behavior.

sentences.text: Shared primitives address different jobs: AGENTS.md carries project guidance, while Agent Skills package reusable procedures.
MCP connects external systems; Agent Client Protocol connects editors and agents; A2A connects independent agent applications.
sentences.spoken: M C P connects external systems; Agent Client Protocol connects editors and agents; A two A connects independent agent applications.

sentences.text: That last boundary is not a prescription for an agent's internal subagents.
Shared formats do not establish identical discovery rules, execution policies, or safety guarantees.

onScreen.text: AGENTS.md: project guidance | Agent Skills: reusable procedures | MCP: external systems | ACP: Agent Client Protocol, editor ↔ agent | A2A: independent agent ↔ independent agent, not internal subagent scheduling · shared formats do not guarantee identical discovery, policy, or safety · as of 2026-10-08

scenes.title: Keep the map dated
scenes.visual: 1.7.1: timeline flips Windsurf to Devin Desktop, then Kimi CLI to Kimi Code CLI; place Roo Code in a retired lane. Show only verified milestones: Devin launch date, Kimi legacy final-release date, and Roo's undated-year shutdown wording rather than inventing a release date. 1.7.2: hold the historical/retired label, not a recommendation button.

sentences.text: The map changes: Windsurf became Devin Desktop, Kimi CLI gave way to Kimi Code CLI, and Roo Code's documentation now reports its extension shut down.
Historical names therefore need historical labels, rather than an active recommendation.

sentences.text: omp's repository describes an open-source, multi-provider Pi fork built by Stencil Labs.
Its integrated tool surface includes language-server tooling, debugger access, structured subagents, and memory.
Those categories are not exclusive; compare dated capabilities and boundaries, not just product names.
